chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir, from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

«Going out on the day of Fitri (Eid al-Fitr) and Adha (Eid al-Adha) to the prayer ground is recommended for whoever is able to go to it.» I asked, «What do you think if he is sick and cannot go out? Should he pray in his house?» He said, «No.» Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning of his saying «No» is that it is not obligatory upon him. And if he were to pray alone in his house, he would deserve the reward, according to what we have previously mentioned in the narrations, and it confirms what we said, what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to go to the mosque for Eid prayers if one is sick?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the Imam’s negative response ('no') to the question of obligation signifies that praying at home is not mandatory (wajib) for the sick, though it remains highly meritorious (mustahabb) as confirmed by other narrations. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the communal aspect of Eid prayers while accommodating individual circumstances without negating spiritual reward.
